text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Chancellor Kohl and parliamentary opposition leader Lafontaine ready for talks to discuss cooperation on tax reform
- Swine fever spreads
- Metallgesellschaft and former chief executive Schimmelbusch approach solution of dispute over oil deals
- Origin of cow infected with BSE remains unclear
- Unions consider consensus talks with Chancellor Kohl on employment
- Pension system administration costs could be much lower, report says
HANDELSBLATT
- Government and pensions experts to present proposals for reform of pensions system
- More new cars registered in 1996
- Finance Ministry state secretary Stark convinced Germany will meet criteria for monetary union in 1999
- Import prices outpaced export prices in 1995
- Chancellor Kohl ready to talk to churches and unions on tax reform
- Survey suggests consumer spending remains restrained
- Germany and France ready to start talks on joint use of French nuclear deterrent
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Chancellor Kohl's Christian Democrats give ground in row with Labour Minister Norbert Bluem over reform of pensions system
- Germany may have first confirmed death from BSE-related Creutzfeld-Jakob disease
- IG Metall engineering union chairman Klaus Zwickel proposes foreigners' quota on labour market
- Steel prices rising again
- VW and Opel GM lose car market share to Mercedes
DIE WELT
- Labour Minister Bluem takes hard line in pensions row
- Fatal case of Creutzfeld-Jakob disease may have been caused by BSE
- Economic research institutes fear losing grants
- Transport Minister Wissmann opposed to increase in state financing for high-speed Transrapid train
- IG Metall engineering union chairman Klaus Zwickel proposes foreigners' quota on labour market
- Unions protest sharply against Bonn tax reform plans
- Skilled trades association demands preferential VAT rate
